All13 Term type classes and reference-resource representations remain unchanged. Boolean/tag/result/error-domain partition proofs therefore remain valid; no new scalar predicate branch exists.
ProcessContext adds only independent SchedulerBinding state. Self/Runtime/Node identity, cancellation token, source-image flow and term arguments are not reassigned by this addition.

RuntimeProcessTaskScheduler still holds immutable Owner and executes captured Task via TryExecuteTask. RuntimeActorExecutionTurn extends the scoped ThreadStatic record with lane identity while setting/restoring the same owner and epoch; migration, queue movement and stealing move scheduler objects, not task/call contexts.

ModuleRegistry selected callback/error-handler lease and actual executing-turn gate are unchanged. Same-owner inline admission still checks IsOwnedBy(Owner); queued Task invokes its previously captured context/body. Lane workers suppress ambient ExecutionContext, while Task restores its captured flow.

Initializer becomes an explicit actor role; its owned context is still the original init ProcessContext and installation Work is processed with the same ThreadStatic current marker and finally restoration. This changes Default-scheduler HOST observations, so old HOST contracts require explicit migration, not weakening guest self/node identity.

New scheduler flag/topology controls can park or resume an owner but do not change an executing predicate argument or owner identity. Cancellation/retirement cleanup and offline lane ordering still require final meaningful focused/full validation; no broad scheduler timing/parity certification follows from preserving16 scalar contracts.

Carries actual runtime capacity to request parsing; keeps local vs disconnected setup context.

Queues store RuntimeProcessTaskScheduler owners; lane routing/cleanup must not substitute another process context.
Control requests retain their initiating ProcessContext and admitted/completed ownership while lanes change.
System flag/query path invokes topology mutation; bind this externally callable entry into owner scheduling state rather than only its helper.
